speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to begin our assessment, please describe the onset, location, and any changes in size or appearance since it first appeared. Additionally, do you have any fever, chills, or recent history of insect bites or trauma to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis secondary to an ant bite, exacerbated by immunosuppression from Crohn's disease and prior corticosteroid use for uveitis.

Please confirm if you have traveled to endemic regions (e.g., Mediterranean, Central/South America, or parts of Asia/Africa) in the last year, and if you have noticed any systemic symptoms like night sweats or weight loss. REQUEST IMAGES: [Skin_Lesion_Right_Leg]
